subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (FinPay)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (FinPay)

Hi Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we heard:
- Primary use: real-time fraud-scoring for payments (low-latency inference called synchronously from your transaction path).
- Current peak: ~30 concurrent requests, spiky around payroll/time-bound batch windows.
- Latency target: P95 < 150ms for 512-token responses; availability target 99.9%.
- Data sensitivity: payment metadata + PII; would prefer private networking for PCI-adjacent workloads.

Key qualification questions we wanted to confirm (you mentioned some on the call):
1) How strict is the 150ms P95 SLA for the first phase vs later phases?
2) Are you willing to run a short pilot on Dedicated capacity if we can show isolation benefits?
3) Any procurement constraints (POs, SOC2 artifacts) on timeline?

Short answers from our side:
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — good for proof-of-concept; we do not guarantee isolated noisy-neighbor-free capacity on shared tier.
- Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools with throughput/latency SLOs and isolation guarantees; recommended for synchronous low-latency workloads at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) — for strict network/data residency or air-gapped requirements.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to share a short note on isolation SLOs and what Dedicated guarantees versus shared.
- I'll send SOC2 summary and the runtime architecture diagram (attached).
- Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ops team this week.

Can you confirm the procurement timeline and whether you can do a pilot on Dedicated in March?

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks for the recap, Priyom — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications below: 

1) SLA & latency: The 150ms P95 is a hard requirement for checkout flows. For background scoring we can tolerate up to 300ms, but checkout is non-negotiable.
2) Pilot: We are open to a dedicated pilot (2–4 weeks) if it can show consistent P95 < 150ms under realistic traffic. Budget sign-off for a pilot is possible in early March.
3) Security/procurement: We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a network architecture diagram to circulate to procurement. Also, do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest?

On noisy-neighbor concerns: we heard from another vendor that even with dedicated pools, there can be shared-host OS effects. Can you confirm what isolation boundaries Redwood guarantees at the Dedicated layer?

I'll set up a tentative deep-dive with our infra lead Jordan for Friday morning PST — will confirm availability.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finpay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (FinPay)

Hi Alex — quick technical answers to the isolation/noisy-neighbor questions (short version):

- Dedicated capacity: provides tenant-level GPU reservation (no multi-tenant model processes on the same GPU). We guarantee compute isolation at the GPU level and control plane policies that prevent resource contention from other customers' inference jobs.
- Host-level isolation: VMs or bare-metal hosts are partitioned by customer; kernel-level noisy-neighbor effects are significantly reduced compared to shared. For extremely strict isolation needs we also offer Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments.
- Tail latency SLOs: For Dedicated we offer SLOs on P95 and P99 latency per model/route based on provisioned capacity. We publish historical percentiles on the Console and can run a 48–72 hour benchmark during a pilot.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: We support model-variant routing (auto-fallback to a smaller model or lower-precision quantized variant) plus circuit-breaker policies. That reduces user-facing errors during transient degradation.

I'll attach a short architecture diagram (redwood-runtime-architecture.png) and a one-pager that outlines the Dedicated guarantees. For KMS: yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments and in Dedicated via a bring-your-key integration — we'll share integration docs in the deep-dive.

If it helps, we can include a simple load profile you give us and run a short soak test on a Dedicated pool with identical request patterns to validate P95 behavior.

Best,
Marissa
